author: zstone1
body:
##### Motivation for this change
I need to deal with monotone, continuous `R->R` functions in homotopy theory. Thankfully, much of it already exists. However, when this was written we didn't have a nice way to talk about behavior at the endpoints of intervals. With the subspace topology infrastructure, we can clean this all up. All changed theorem have been improved:

- Many conditions weaken from `{in I, continuous f}` to `{within I, continuous f}`. The problem is `{ in [a,b], continuous f}` relies on f being continuous _from the left_ at `a`. That's bad news, because it depends on values outside of `[a,b]`. Instead `{within I, continuous f}` truly doesn't care about values outside of `I`. 
- Many of the results strengthen from `{in ]a, b[, continuous f}` to `{within [a,b], continuous f}`, which is _slightly_ stronger by controlling the "from-the-right" continuity at `a`, and dually at `b`. The original result can be recovered with a `continuous_subspaceW` + `open_continuous_subspace`.
 
Several of the theorems that strengthen the result from `{in ]a, b[, continuous f}` to `{within [a,b], continuous f}` are pretty tricky. The endpoints require a lot of annoying interval arithmetic to get right, but I did end up finding a way.

body:
According to published usage, transposed chords (bII, etc.) should take their 7th from the key and not be transposed.  So in c-minor, bII7 should be D-, F, A-, C, and not with C-flat.

Assuming that this would apply to 9ths, 11ths, and 13ths as well.

Does not affect interpretation of vi7, VI7, etc., I don't believe.

Slows the creation of bII, etc. RomanNumerals because a new Chord object needs to be created temporarily and `_findRoot()` run on it.

Add a new chord.tools file for routines that are too obscure to go on Chord.  Created `chord.tools.getAllChordSteps`

Fixes #1410

Credit MalcolmSailor for the notice and research on this.

author: zacharycmontoya
body:
## Summary of changes
Adds support for instrumenting interface methods and updates an existing RabbitMQ integration to use it.

Note: Due to the metadata available at module load time (where we dictate what types/methods need to be instrumented via ReJIT), we can only instrument types that directly implement the specified interface. If a type indirectly implements via inheritance, we cannot instrument it via interface instrumentation and we must specify a derived instrumentation on the base class. This limitation has been documented in `docs/development/AutomaticInstrumentation.md`.

## Reason for change
This fills a gap in instrumentation when an API we want to instrument is defined on an interface type (like RabbitMQ's BasicDeliver method), since an application may supply its own type. While the gap used to be purely theoretical, we have seen some users now hit this gap so it's important to address.

## Implementation details

### Integration changes
- Updated the RabbitMQ `BasicDeliverIntegration` in the following ways:
  - Removed direct instrumentation on `RabbitMQ.Client.Events.EventingBasicConsumer.HandleBasicDeliver`
  - Added interface instrumentation on `RabbitMQ.Client.IBasicConsumer.HandleBasicDeliver`
  - Added derived instrumentation on `RabbitMQ.Client.DefaultBasicConsumer.HandleBasicDeliver` (this implements the above interface)
    - This is the primary base class used by other internal classes, so this instrumentation is required when `HandleBasicDeliver` is overridden by a derived class
- Added a new RabbitMQ `BasicDeliverAsyncIntegration`:
  - Added interface instrumentation on `RabbitMQ.Client.IAsyncBasicConsumer.HandleBasicDeliver`
  - Added derived instrumentation on `RabbitMQ.Client.AsyncDefaultBasicConsumer.HandleBasicDeliver` (this implements the above interface)
    - This is the primary base class used by other internal classes, so this instrumentation is required when `HandleBasicDeliver` is overridden by a derived class
- Also added a small check to avoid nested RabbitMQ spans, which could happen if both the interface instrumentation and derived instrumentation occurs

### Profiler changes
- Added a new PInvoke `AddInterfaceInstrumentations`
- Updated the integration definition to have a new field `is_interface` (since this requires unique handling)
- Implement interface instrumentation...

### Instrumentation logic
Instrumentation occurs in two phases: 1) For a given integration definition, we iterate the loaded modules to determine which types require instrumentation, and then 2) The type is scanned for a method name matching the integration definition and marked for ReJIT if a matching method is found.

#### Iterating loaded modules

1. When the integration definition is marked as an interface instrumentation, we iterate over every single type in the module.
2. We get a list of interfaces that the type implements (supplied by the assembly that defines the type)
3. If one of the interface types matches the name listed in the integration definition, the type is marked for rewriting and its methods will be scanned for the corresponding method.

#### Matching methods
1. The first part of the method matching remains unchanged: we get a list of methods whose names exactly match the method name in the integration definition, and instrument only those whose signatures match.
2. If the integration definition is an interface instrumentation, then we also get a list of explicit interface methods (`InterfaceFullName.MethodName`) and attempt to match those as well.

## Test coverage
- Added tests to the `CallTargetsNative` project to test the basic operation of instrumenting an interface method
- Added more consumer types in the `Samples.RabbitMQ` to test exercise various scenarios and significantly refactored the sample for better clarity
- Updated `InstrumentationDefinitionsGeneratorTests.cs` to test that the updated integration code-gen is correct


## Other details
N/A

author: dairiki
body:
Following up on [this suggestion] made in a comment on #169 (see also #210), this provides a new schema method, `.load_to_mapping`, that essentially does a raw `marshmallow.Schema.load` without converting any of the deserialized values (either top-level or nested) to dataclasses.  The main point of this is to allow for deserializing partial data (with `partial=True`).

This PR is provided for discussion, as to:
- whether it's worthwhile
- whether there's a better name for the new method
- whether there's a better way to implement the new method
- ...

[this suggestion]: https://github.com/lovasoa/marshmallow_dataclass/issues/169#issuecomment-1256298997

A couple of efficiency improvements
- Check if contract code hash is equal to the empty hash, and do not bother to call `eth_getCode` if so
- Add `from`, `to`, and `payload.fee_recipient` to the access list of every call so the account fetch can be parallelized

These changes bring making the giant Uniswap balance fetch multicall down from 2.5 seconds to 1.5 seconds
